summary: Backend testing for v0.12.0-beta GDPR compliance MVP. Created /app/backend/tests/test_gdpr_v012.py with 20 pytest cases. Result: 17/20 PASS, 3/20 FAIL. All authenticated GDPR endpoints in routes/gdpr.py are BROKEN due to two systemic coding bugs: (1) `user['_id']` is used but core.auth.get_current_user() returns user['id'] (string) after popping '_id' — causes KeyError '_id' on every authenticated GDPR call; (2) `_log_audit(user, 'action', details=...)` is called with an invalid kwarg 'details' and missing required positional 'target_type'. Publicly visible endpoints (privacy, cookie, termini, versioni, impostazioni-sindacato GET, register consent enforcement, /gdpr/registro-trattamenti, RBAC 403, /version, non-regression on login/me/rimborsi/sedi/notifiche) ALL WORK CORRECTLY.

critical.issue: 500 KeyError '_id' — routes/gdpr.py:166 uses user['_id'] but get_current_user() pops '_id' and sets 'id' (string). Fix: user_id = ObjectId(user['id']).

500 KeyError '_id' at gdpr.py:209 (user_id = ObjectId(user['_id'])). Same root cause. Additionally, gdpr.py:234 calls _log_audit(user, 'gdpr.richiesta_cancellazione', details={...}) — invalid signature (missing target_type, no 'details' kwarg).
500 KeyError '_id' at gdpr.py:246. Also _log_audit(user, 'gdpr.annulla_cancellazione') at L253 is missing required target_type param.

500 TypeError: _log_audit() got an unexpected keyword argument 'details' (gdpr.py:117). _log_audit signature is (actor, action, target_type, target_id=..., target_label=..., ...). Must pass target_type='impostazioni' and use note=json.dumps(data) or similar.

action_items: FIX routes/gdpr.py: replace every occurrence of user['_id'] with ObjectId(user['id']) — 4 locations (L166, L209, L246, L262). Note the model already has user['id'] as a string from get_current_user.

FIX routes/gdpr.py: update all 3 _log_audit() calls to match core/audit.py signature. Current signature requires positional target_type; 'details' kwarg does not exist. Suggested replacements: L117 -> _log_audit(user, 'impostazioni.update', target_type='impostazioni', target_id='singleton', note=str(data)); L234 -> _log_audit(user, 'gdpr.richiesta_cancellazione', target_type='user', target_id=user['id'], target_label=user['email'], note=payload.motivo); L253 -> _log_audit(user, 'gdpr.annulla_cancellazione', target_type='user', target_id=user['id'], target_label=user['email']).
Retest after fix: 3 failing test cases in test_gdpr_v012.py should turn green.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/gdpr.py has ZERO integration test coverage before deploy — 5 endpoints (all authenticated GDPR paths) 500-crash on first call. This is a regression-testing gap; the router was added without smoke-testing any authenticated endpoint locally.

routes/gdpr.py:166,209,246,262: pattern user['_id'] appears 4x. Root cause is developer assuming core.auth returns raw Mongo dict; but it deliberately maps _id -> id (string). Suggest adding a linter/CI rule or a helper get_user_oid(user) that centralizes ObjectId(user['id']).

routes/gdpr.py:117,234,253: _log_audit() calls all use non-existent 'details' kwarg — copy-paste from a different signature. Compare with routes/rimborsi.py or routes/users.py for correct usage pattern.
core/legal_templates.py:104 mentions grace period of 30 giorni — matches richiedi-cancellazione code path (+timedelta(days=30)). GOOD alignment.
gdpr.py:282 get_registro_trattamenti WORKS correctly (returns 4 trattamenti + titolare) — proves the router itself loads and RBAC works.
gdpr.py `get_settings()` creates default doc on first read — safe, idempotent. Verified via test_public_get_returns_correct_data returning Rapallo address + CF 91027960102.
GDPR consenso in auth/register.py:95-104 correctly persists to db.consensi_privacy with email/version/timestamp/ip/user-agent — verified by test_register_with_both_creates_consenso.
auth/register.py:47 correctly blocks registration with HTTP 400 when either privacy_accepted or termini_accepted is False — verified by two dedicated tests.
seed_data_creation: Test users prefixed test_gdpr_* created via /api/auth/register; consensi_privacy and richieste_cancellazione records auto-created. Session-scoped cleanup fixture removes them by regex ^test_gdpr_ from users, consensi_privacy, richieste_cancellazione at start and end of run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: After main agent fixes the two systemic bugs (user['_id'] -> ObjectId(user['id']) and _log_audit signature) in routes/gdpr.py, rerun: `python -m pytest /app/backend/tests/test_gdpr_v012.py -v`. All 20 tests should pass. The cleanup fixture is session-scoped and idempotent, so re-runs are safe. hCaptcha is disabled (HCAPTCHA_SECRET empty in .env) — register works without token. Login/register set httpOnly cookies with samesite=none, secure=true; requests.Session() handles them automatically. Non-regression suite (login, /auth/me, /sedi, /rimborsi, /notifiche) is included and all PASSED — v0.12.0-beta did not break v0.11.4 endpoints.

rca of the issue: TWO SYSTEMIC BUGS in routes/gdpr.py introduced with v0.12.0-beta GDPR router: (A) get_current_user() in core/auth.py:91-92 explicitly does user['id']=str(user['_id']); user.pop('_id', None). Therefore accessing user['_id'] inside gdpr.py endpoints raises KeyError. Fix: use ObjectId(user['id']) everywhere. Affects gdpr.py lines 166, 209, 246, 262. (B) core/audit.py _log_audit() signature is (actor, action, target_type, target_id=..., target_label=..., sede_id=..., old_value=..., new_value=..., note=...). It does NOT accept a 'details' kwarg. gdpr.py calls it with kwarg details=... at lines 117, 234, 253 — raises TypeError. All 5 authenticated GDPR endpoints affected. REPRODUCTION: authenticate as any user, GET /api/gdpr/my-data → 500 KeyError. As superadmin, PUT /api/impostazioni-sindacato with any body → 500 TypeError _log_audit unexpected keyword 'details'. MITIGATION for main agent: apply the two mechanical rewrites listed in action_items.
